headline: Discussed $500,000 request for Elementary school HVAC replacement; approved Burbank Road pole move.
summary: Officials heard that the Elementary school and ELC heating, ventilation, and air systems are past their useful life, and that some classrooms fell below the state's 68-degree standard for special education rooms. The Town Manager asked for $500,000 for design work and an owner's project manager, and estimated the full project at up to $3.5 million. The board also appointed Jessica Clement to the Cultural Council.
decisions: Approved the August 18, 2026 meeting minutes, 3-0 with one abstention.
Approved the August 25, 2026 meeting minutes, 3-0 with one abstention.
Approved Pole Hearing #31347068 from NGrid and Verizon New England for Burbank Road, 4-0 roll call vote.
Appointed Jessica Clement to the Cultural Council, with a term to expire June 30, 2029, 4-0 roll call vote.

                                                                                             6:00 p.m. –  September 8, 2026                  
   HYBRID MEETING Roll Call vote taken:
Members in Attendance:
Chairperson Anderson, Vice Chair Ettamarna, Select members Watkins and Spengler all present in person (Limanek will zoom in 
when available)
Also attending in person: Town Manager Austin Cyganiewicz & Deb Jacques, secretary
Public Forum – 
Jim Lehner 27 Uxbridge Road- Mr. Lehner discusses the excessive speed vehicles travel on Uxbridge Road. He would like to see the 
speed reduced to 30MPH as well as the sign at Bond Hollow that says dead end should be moved as it confuses drivers if they are not 
familiar with the area. The Police Dept. have been called a few times but Mr. Lehner feels if the Police sat on the road with radar it 
would send a message to the drivers. Town Manager Cyganiewicz reviews the way speed limits are changed. It is through the state not
town and there would need to be traffic studies and data submitted to the state but we will reach out to the PD as well. 
John Belculfine 75 Leland Hill Road- agrees that the speed in town is an issue on his road way- 77 communities have adopted 25 
MPH for thickly settled areas. Also an issue are the motorized ebikes and scooters. Per bylaw 25- electric scooters are not allowed in 
town. 
Andrea Mattei 21 Golf Ridge Drive- agrees speeds should be lowered. Andrea is here requesting a status update of the amendment 
with Unified – lot 1. It was discussed at the Dec 2025 meeting and then again at the March 2026 meeting.  Town Mgr. Cyganiewicz 
replies he will come back at the next meeting with an update- the EACC meets quarterly- so he believes they met in June but he would
like to pull up the results to get the actual information. Andrea states she would like it to be very clear in the documents that lot 1 is 
out. 
Select person Watkins motions to accept as presented the August 18, 2026 Select Board meeting minutes as presented, Vice Chair 
Ettamarna seconds passes 3-0 and 1 abstention - Watkins “aye”, Ettamarna abstains, Spengler “aye” Anderson “aye”
Select person Watkins motions to accept as presented the August 25, 2026 Select Board minutes as presented Vice Chair Ettamarna

*Public Pole Hearing*  Burbank Road hearing read into record by Select Watkins- present on Zoom is Evan Loosigand with NGrid. 
Mr. Loosigand replies this is being moved for a new driveway and service to 124 & 126 Burbank Road. Vice Chair Ettamarna states 
Police, Fire and Highway have all given the ok. Resident Todd Clark 134 Burbank Road wants clarification that the pole is not being 
moved closer to his driveway- it is clarified it is moving further away from his property. Hearing no concerns- Vice Chair Ettamarna 
motions to close the Public Hearing Select Watkins seconds passes 4-0 with roll call vote. Vice Chair Ettamarna motions to approve 
Pole Hearing # 31347068 from NGrid & Verizon New England for Burbank Road as advertised in the August 18, 2026 Millbury 
Sutton Chronicle Select Watkins seconds passes 4-0 with roll call vote- Watkins “aye”, Ettamarna “aye”, Spengler “aye” Anderson 
“aye”
Cultural Council appointment- Jessica Clement- Jessica has lived in town since 2020- she is involved with the PTO, girl scouts and 
works at Boston Children’s Hospital. She wishes to broaden her involvement through the culture in town. The Select Board all offer 
their appreciation for her wishing to volunteer her time. Select Spengler motions to appoint Jessica Clement to the Cultural Council 
with a term to expire June 30, 2029 Select Watkins seconds passes 4-0 with roll call vote- Watkins “aye”, Ettamarna “aye”, Spengler 
“aye” Anderson “aye”
www.suttonma.gov
Assessor’s Office –Review Sr. Tax Work off Policy- Town Mgr. Cyganiewicz requests to postpone this to a later date for further 
review. 
Simonian/Elementary HVAC project Update- present is Superintendent Caitlyn Paget along with Town Mgr. Cyganiewicz to present 
slideshow. Town Mgr. Cyganiewicz begins with a request of $500,000. Borrowing to fund an Owners Project Mgr. and 
design/engineering services to bring the HVAC replacement project to bid ready specifications.  HVAC is the last major system to be 
addressed to sustain the life of the ELC/Elem. A recent report by CSI Engineering shows most of the mechanical equipment is past its 
useful life. Overall the condition of these buildings are in good to excellent condition according to CSI.  This was going to be a project
thru the MSBA but due to certain things (required to replace the roof on ELC when not needed) that would have increased the cost it 
was decided to not go thru the MSBA.  School Administration noted several class rooms fell below the Mass DESE regulations of 
maintaining classroom temperatures at 68 degrees for the special ed placements. There is not a specific regulation for general ed 
students. The winter of 24/25 & 25/26 showed heating issues in the ELC with some rooms in the 50’s. Classes were relocated to the 
library and emergency short term repairs were performed. There are 4 roof top units’ air handling units and exhaust fans that are 
approx. 28+ years old (ELC- 50+ yrs/Elem 28 yrs old). The Elementary school received a chiller in 2022 thru capital plan that is in 
excellent condition.  Superintendent Paget states we are band aiding a problem that requires a full HVAC replacement. The 
Town/District has invested close to 1 million dollars on HVAC repairs between FY2022-FY2027. The estimated cost for 
maintenance/repairs over the next 15 years is approx. 3 million dollars. The Select Board question some of the expenses for the 
Upkeep and Repairs over the past 5 years showing the HVAC repairs & maintenance such as the difference in cost for software 
vendors for the ELC/Elem vs the M/H schools. Select Watkins states there is 152,000 sq. feet in the Elem/ELC and 179,000 sq. feet in
the Midd/High School- there is a big disparity in the cost to the Elem/ELC software and it is a smaller sq. footage. Caitlyn will request
more information for the board. Superintendent Paget reviews the change in student population- the number of students has declined 
but the students with needs has increased. This increase in needs increases the dedicated space required for services as well as staff. 
Select Watkins questions how that relates to space standards under the CLR.  How would we get a handle on that with the growth and 
the sq. footage and the decline in population? Christine says DESE sets mandates but does not provide additional funding. Christine 
asks if Caitlyn could call DESE to get the actual sq. footage required for our school population. Vice Chair Ettamarna comments on 
the complex & diverse reality- over 30% of the kids require special needs- there are 4 different populations- how do we serve 
everybody without increasing space for one population. Will we get to the point where the increased needs for some of the kids pushes
out Prek? Caitlyn replies it is her goal to expand prek because it is a revenue generating program. Chair Anderson says what exactly 
are the space requirements and what do we need. We have a declining enrollment. Should we spend all this money, should we upgrade
the building. This building has plenty of life left in it- it is not time to think about replacing it. Come to us with a list of all the things 
that are going on that need to be fixed vs piece meal. Select. Spengler says when classes are displaced due to the conditions it is a 
school day going by with a fraction of the educational value that these kids should be getting. The fraction is less than 50% which is 
not acceptable. Caitlyn agrees that is lost time. Dan says that is important for residents to know going forward. Vice Chair Ettamarna 
says that is what is called a snow day. Superintendent Paget says there are going to be things that reach end of life and we should have 
thought about it years ago. It’s important that if we do go forward with this and replace the HVAC system at both locations we need to
start planning. Vice Chair Ettamarna states something could have an expected useful life but that all depends on the moving parts and 
the various specifics of the system. There are plenty of well-engineered well-built things that its life can be extended and run well 
beyond that time. Who in your team has the operational responsibilities and the accountability to make sure we are overseeing this. 
Select. Watkins says if we do the HVAC now- how does that phase in with the water treatment, the sewer treatment. How are we 
supposed to look at all the assets of the municipality – Austin has pointed out we have issues with many of the buildings- the school is 
one of the buildings- how do we have to decide how to allocate our funds and if we have to ask for more we have to have an idea of 
what that is because we can’t ask all the time. How do we prioritize if we do not have all the data? Is this going to be debt exclusion- 
is the $500,000. Borrowing? Austin replies we will ask for borrowing authorization on the $500,000. to be funded through the FY28 
funding. Austin states based on the assessment by CSI they gave an estimate based on quantity and labor totaling just over 2.6 million-
Austin took that with some other information and compared to similar projects in Millbury and BVT and so we are estimating this 
project to be up to 3.5 Million (this includes escalation as we do not know the time line for the project).  Vice Chair Ettamarna wants 
to see the root causes mentioned when the report comes out- what can be salvaged, what is good. Maybe look in to grant funding as 
ways to get the funding to fix these things. Don’t go crazy on the system-scope it the right way.  Chair Anderson says we have to have
in the forefront will we be able to have these systems last for 2 winters before the project could begin. Discussion continued. 
Select person Limanek joins the meeting via ZOOM at 7:20 pm
Town Manager Update:
 Wilkinsonville Water District Draft Water Management Act Permit- MADEP issued Wilks Water an additional 100,000 
gallons per day in permitted volume flow. Attached is the draft permit with conditions. Suttons Community Development 
Office did submit comments to MADEP requesting a correction of a misstatement that we do not have a drain bylaw- Sutton 
Does have a floor drain control bylaw. 
 City Health Dashboard- this is a tool developed by the NYU Grossman School of Medicines Dept. of Population Health. This
provides data from a variety of sources across state and federal agencies. This is to provide public health data. Once it is fully
implemented it will be shared with the community.
www.suttonma.gov
 FY2027 Budget and Fall Town Meeting Warrant- The Assessor’s office has informed us we will have a positive impact on 
FY27 and future budgets with an additional $600,000. In new growth to the personal & commercial tax levy classes. This 
still needs to be certified by DOR
 Midstate Massive Ultra Trail event- annual event October 10-11- between 250-300 runners. The Police will provide details.
 Speed Limits on Roadways- as discussed during Public Forum speed limits are governed by the state
 Sibley Rd & Burbank Rd intersection- a resident on Burbank Rd has requested a formal engineer review. Funds were 
approved in FY2023 Capital Plan for this traffic study. 
Select Board Round Table
Select person Limanek enters the meeting room at 8:23 in person
Vice Chair Ettamarna mentions the meeting he and Select Spengler had with Erin and Austin regarding the Town Manager Review. 
Jim says they should time Austin’s review to be in line with the other town employee reviews. This would allow them to synchronize 
all the town Dept Head reviews and have Austin’s flow off of that. Dan comments that it flows better with the Budget season. Jim says
the Board can give Austin their individual reviews this year so he has a pulse check. Then have the official review the end of 
June/July. Jim also likes the idea of pulse survey of the employees thru a survey. Soccer kicked off today at the Sutton Schools.
Select Watkins – an email from CMMPO re. a meeting they would like a Select Board member to attend. It is ZOOM- Christine is the 
CMRPC rep and would be happy to attend this meeting. Also an invite (zoom) in Dec. to discuss the Municipal Land Mass study. 
Christine will attend. Waters Farm is holding an auction on 9/19 and apple peeling for Waters farm will be Sept. 12th at the 1st
Congregational Church. 
Select Limanek reads the list of items needed for the Sutton Food Pantry as well as where they can be dropped off. Sat 9/12 at the

was the SE rep the last 8 years- he is stepping down next Wed. will be his last meeting. This will leave the position available to 
another Select Board member in the SE region.
